string.text: Brenin Wulf rules the wild clans of Dunland with an iron fist. Known as the Ironhand, he united the scattered hill tribes through conquest and cunning. He dreams of reclaiming the lands taken by the Horse-lords of Rohan.
Aranel, wife of Elphir, is a noble lady of Gondor known for her dignity and keen mind.
Ciryandur commands the northern defenses of Gondor, a seasoned veteran of many orc raids. He is methodical and relentless in defending the borders of the realm.
Elarwen, wife of Hirgon, is a woman of the borders known for her resilience and practical wisdom.
Findariel, wife of Ciryandur, manages the affairs of their household with care and intelligence.
The Mouth of Sauron speaks with the Dark Lord's authority. Once a Black Numenorean, he has forgotten his own name after ages of service to evil. He commands the garrison of the Black Gate.
The Witch-King of Angmar, Lord of the Nazgûl, is Sauron's most terrible servant. He was once a great king of Men, corrupted by his Ring of Power into an undying wraith.
The Dark Marshall commands the Nazgûl in battle, second only to the Witch-King.
The Knight of Umbar was once a lord of the Corsairs before taking the Ring.

Sauron the Great, Dark Lord of Mordor and Lord of the Rings, has risen again. From the black tower of Barad-dûr his Eye sweeps the lands of the West, and the legions of Gorgoroth muster beneath his banner. The Free Peoples reckoned him beaten, but the Shadow only bided its time. Now he marches to break them and bind all of Middle-earth under one dominion. Let the kings of Men despair, for the age of Sauron is come.

Khorgath serves as a high officer in the armies of Mordor, a son of Sauron raised to the muster of war. He drives his legions toward the lands of Men with the cold patience of one who knows the Eye is always watching.
Morgha stands at the Dark Lord's side, mistress of the inner hierarchy of Lugbúrz. Her word carries the weight of the Eye, and the captains of Mordor fear her counsel as much as Sauron's wrath.
Eldith Grey-Claw is a fierce warrior woman of Dunland, renowned for her ferocity in battle.
Haldis Redmist leaves a trail of blood wherever she rides into battle.
Yrla Ghostpelt wears the skin of a white wolf, said to grant her protection in battle.
Freya Clawrend leads a warband of fierce shield-maidens into battle. She trained as a warrior from childhood and has never known defeat.
Gundrun Ironpaw is a veteran warrior with hands scarred by countless sword grips.
Morgith is a mysterious figure who communes with the spirits of the ancient hills.
Aelwyn Hawkeye commands a company of hill scouts who patrol the borders.
Brianna Wingdart learned archery from her mother and now surpasses her in skill.
Branoc Feathershaft is the finest archer among the Dunlendings, able to shoot the eye out of a raven at a hundred paces.
Sigga Wyrmbane earned her name slaying a great serpent in the mountain passes.
Sigrun Boarfang is known for her fearless charges into enemy ranks.
Thyra Bloodtusk earned her epithet through countless victories.
Hilda Bonecrusher is feared for her devastating strength in combat.
Yrsa the Winter Boar leads raids during the harshest seasons when enemies least expect attack.
Freydis Oxmane is wife to Othric and a skilled healer as well as warrior.
Eira Shadowclaw moves silently through enemy camps, striking without warning.
Sifra Bonewalker walks among the fallen after battle, collecting trophies from the slain.
Freya Wolfheart is the fierce wife of Brenin Wulf. She commands respect among the warriors for her skill with axe and shield.
Astrid Bearclaw is known for her ferocious fighting style and bear-skin cloak.
Fenrik the Red Wolf leads raiding parties deep into enemy territory.
Bjornric Strongarm is a mighty warrior who wields a great war axe in battle.
Caladwen, wife of Erchirion, joined the house of Imrazôrionath through their union. She is a woman of quiet courage.
Amrothos, youngest son of Imrahil, is still young but already shows his family's martial spirit and noble character.
Elphir, eldest son of Imrahil, is heir to Dol Amroth. He commands the Swan Knights with martial precision and carries his father's noble bearing.
Hirgon, brother of Ciryandur, serves as an errand-rider of Gondor. Swift and reliable, he carries messages between the lords of the realm.
Nûlubêth is a Black Numenorean sorceress in service to the Dark Tower. Her name means Night-Word in the old Adunaic speech, and she chose it herself.
Aganuzîr leads the raiding parties that ride west of the Black Gate. His name means Death-Lover, and his mother intended it as a blessing.
Ugruphel rides with her brother's raiders and keeps the tally of everything they take. She has never seen the sea her ancestors crossed.
Ugrukhôr holds the wall-walk of the Morannon for the Mouth of Sauron. He is of the old Black Numenorean blood, and he counts the Orcs under his command as tools rather than soldiers.
The Betrayer was once a king in the East before his corruption.
Herumarth, a Black Númenórean of Sauron's own blood, commands a fortress on the marches of Mordor. Cold and proud, he keeps the old Númenórean cruelty sharpened by the Shadow that sired him.
Gorwulf the Boar is a savage chieftain known for his brutal raids on border settlements.
Gothmog, Lieutenant of Morgul, commands the armies of Mordor at the Pelennor Fields. A brutal and cunning Orc, he leads from the front.
Svala Redfang is an Orc captain under Gothmog's command.
Mogra serves the dark powers of Mordor.
Snaga is a servant of the Shadow.
Zrsa Blackfang is heir to the Ironhand, eager to prove herself worthy of her father's legacy.
Eldra Boarsong carries on the fierce traditions of her parents.
Brigid the Howling leads war bands through the mountain passes.
Faramir, younger son of Denethor, is Captain of the Rangers of Ithilien. Though overlooked by his father, he is beloved by his men for his wisdom, mercy, and quiet strength.
Erchirion, second son of Imrahil, serves as a knight of Dol Amroth. Bold in battle and loyal to his house, he rides with his father's Swan Knights.
Ivriniel, daughter of Ciryandur, has grown up in the northern marches of Gondor and shows both her father's resilience and her mother's wisdom.
Dolguphel is the daughter of the Mouth of Sauron, though he has long since put aside the title of father. She commands the horse of Carach Angren and studies the arts her house does not name aloud.
The Undying was a sorcerer-king who sought immortality and found only eternal servitude.
Naktharil, daughter of the Dark Lord, is steeped in the dark arts of Dol Guldur and Lugbúrz. She walks the Shadow's hidden roads, and those who cross her are not heard from again.
Brunhild Ironclaw is the formidable wife of Gorwulf, equally skilled in battle as her husband.
Borhador, Lord of Barahirionath, is one of the eldest lords of Gondor. His long years have given him wisdom, though his body weakens with age. His counsel is respected by all.
Lindariel, wife of Borhador, has been the strength of their house through many long years. She is a gracious and enduring presence in Gondor's nobility.
Beregund Wolfborn is a trusted captain of Dunland, known for his skill in raiding Rohirric settlements.
Grimwulf Ironfang carries on his father's legacy of raiding and warfare against Rohan.
Hrodgar Ironhide serves as a champion of the clan, his armor scarred by countless battles.
Drengulf Irontusk is a young warrior eager to prove his worth in battle.
Gormund Oxflank serves as a trusted lieutenant to the clan chief.
Nemos is a captain of the Tower Guard, sworn to protect the Steward.
Forlong the Fat, Lord of Lossarnach, leads the largest contingent from the fiefs to the defense of Minas Tirith. Despite his girth, he is a fierce and experienced warrior.
Berethiel, wife of Forlong, is the Lady of Lossarnach. She oversees the fertile valleys while her husband rides to war.
Caldamir, young son of Forlong, has recently come of age and rides to war eager to prove himself.
Rúmil, elder brother of Forlong, is a steady presence in the House of Ausirionath. His long years of service have earned him the respect of his kin.
Malrior, son of Borhador, carries on his father's duties as the old lord ages. He is steady and dependable, respected by his clan.
Thorwen, wife of Malrior, is a capable woman who manages her household with quiet determination.
Zimrabêth speaks for her husband's house at the Black Gate, and speaks rather better than he does. The Mouth of Sauron has found her useful more than once.
Azruphel is fourteen and already rides with the Morannon patrols. Her name means Sea-Daughter, for a sea no living Black Numenorean has laid eyes on.
Abrazîn was named for the old Numenorean virtue of steadfastness. In Mordor the word has come to mean something much closer to obedience.
Ulbar keeps the forges beneath Carach Angren and the slaves who feed them. His is one of the few names his people carried out of Numenor unchanged.
Khamûl the Easterling, second of the Nine, once ruled a great kingdom in Rhun before accepting a Ring of Power.
The Tainted spreads corruption wherever he rides.
The Shadow of the Northmen hunts in the cold lands.
The Shadow of Umbar haunts the southern coasts.
Skarnak leads a company of Mordor orcs, a brutal captain who claws his way up the muster by breaking those above him. The lash and the Eye are the only laws he keeps.
Tristania serves in the dark forces.
Gordiana dwells in the shadow of the Dark Tower.
Othric the Wild is a chieftain whose unpredictable tactics have won him many victories. His clan claims descent from ancient Dunlending kings.
Corwyn Raveneye sees omens in the flight of birds and counsels the clan on matters of war.
Haldric Talonstrike leads ambushes from the high crags.
Hirluin the Fair, Lord of Pinnath Gelin, leads his green-clad warriors from the hills of Gondor. He is known for his valor and loyalty to the Steward.
Anariel, daughter of Hirluin, has grown up among the warriors of Pinnath Gelin and can hold her own in battle.
Barandor, son of Hirluin, trains to one day lead the warriors of Pinnath Gelin. He rides with his father's green-clad company.
Nauriel, wife of Hirluin, is the Lady of Pinnath Gelin, known for her steadfastness and care for the people of the green hills.
Angbor the Fearless, Lord of Lamedon, rallied his men even when the Dead marched through his lands. He is bold and quick to act.
Shagrat, Captain of Cirith Ungol, guards the pass into Mordor. He is known for his cruelty even among Orcs.
Constalia serves in the tower of Cirith Ungol.
Mathmog is a powerful Uruk-hai war chief.
Megethia serves the dark powers.
Tormund the Hammer earned his name through devastating charges with his war hammer.
Gwenna is wife to Tormund, managing the clan's holdings while he campaigns.
Rustica rides to war alongside her father Tormund, a fierce young warrior of the clan.
Baranor serves as a captain in the Lossarnach contingent, a trusted officer of Lord Forlong.
Calathiel, wife of Caldamir, is a young noblewoman of Lossarnach.
Imloth is daughter of Baranor, learning the ways of Gondor's nobility in the valleys of Lossarnach.
Gorvin the Fell is a grim chieftain whose cruelty is legendary even among Dunlendings.
Torvald Oxhorn is the heir of Othric, already showing his father's wild spirit.
Oromar, husband of Anariel, joined the house of Halboronionath through their union. He serves the Lord of Pinnath Gelin faithfully.
Isfin, wife of Barandor, is a woman of the Green Hills known for her grace.
Gorbag, Captain of Minas Morgul, leads the garrison of the dead city. He is cunning even by Orc standards.
Valaria serves in the citadel of the dead.
Comatasa is an Orc bred for war.
Elidilea serves in the dark hierarchy.
Thormund Grizzlyhew cleaves through enemy ranks with his great two-handed axe.
Talric Crowcall can mimic any bird's cry, using them as signals in battle.
Eorwyn Featherbolt prefers the bow to the blade, striking from the shadows.
Gorthak is an orc captain holding the high pass into Mordor, watchful and merciless to any who would slip past the Eye.
Silvina serves in the garrison of the spider's pass.
Grukhash commands a fortress on the borders of Mordor, a wary keeper of the Shadow's marches.
Areliana serves in the borderlands.
Dorathila serves in the dark armies.

Denethor II, Steward of Gondor, rules from the White Tower of Minas Tirith. Once a man of great wisdom, he has grown proud and unyielding. He resists the return of the king, believing only he can save Gondor from the shadow of Mordor.
Veyra the Shadow slips unseen into enemy camps to slit throats in the night.
Golasgil, Lord of Anfalas, commands the long coastline against Corsair raids. He is a weathered sea-lord who has defended Gondor's shores for decades.
Laswen, wife of Golasgil, oversees the coastal settlements of Anfalas while her husband guards the sea lanes.
Bolg is a powerful Orc chieftain, descended from Azog the Defiler.
Viviana serves in the dark hierarchy.
Narmir, younger brother of Angbor, serves in the defense of Lamedon. He shares his brother's courage if not yet his experience.
Belwen, wife of Angbor, stands steadfastly by her husband in the defense of Lamedon.
Bûrznak commands a regiment of Mordor orcs, a mounted captain who rides down stragglers and deserters alike.
Zena serves the dark masters of Mordor.
Boromir, eldest son of Denethor, is Captain-General of Gondor. A great warrior of renown, he seeks any weapon to defend his people against the darkness.
Húrioneth serves the House of Húrinionath, a steadfast keeper of the lore of Gondor's stewards.

Imrahil II, Prince of Dol Amroth, is the greatest knight of Gondor. His line carries Elvish blood, and he is said to be the fairest lord in all the realm. His Swan Knights are legendary throughout Middle-earth.
Lothwen, Princess of Dol Amroth, has stood beside Imrahil through decades of service to Gondor. She is known for her grace and quiet wisdom.
Bard II, King of Dale, is grandson of the legendary Bard the Bowman who slew Smaug. He rules the prosperous kingdom at the foot of Erebor, allied with the Dwarves of the Lonely Mountain.
Valla is a princess of Dale, trained in diplomacy and statecraft.
Idrun is a Dwarf warrior of the royal guard.
Rozhivol is a Dwarf warrior who guards the mountain gates.
Svana is a daughter of the trading house.
Osven manages caravans between the mountain and the city.
Vidar is a lord of the northern marches, guarding against Easterling incursions.
Lilizha is a daughter of a Barding noble house.
Andruta serves in the household of the king.
Luda is a young noblewoman of Dale.
Teta is a noble daughter of Dale.
Isvan is a lord of the eastern marches, guarding the Long Lake.
Valkava is wife to Lord Isvan.
Zaverena is heir to the eastern holdings.
Vizhduna is a young noble of the eastern marches.
Ratagost is a wise counselor who advises the king on matters of state.
Yachana serves in the royal court.
Milanka is a noblewoman of the court.
Velina serves the royal household.
Bovan is a young nobleman of Dale.
Hauk is a lord of Dale, master of the market roads and the winter caravans.
Tyaska is wife to Hauk, skilled in the healing arts.
Stein is a lord of Dale, remembered for holding the northern gate in the years after the dragon fell.
Dracha keeps the memory of the old king alive.
Ulf is a lord of Dale, captain of the river-watch upon the Running River.
Zorika is wife to Ulf, and mistress of his hall upon the Running River.
Geir is a warrior of Dale of great renown, kin to the old line of Girion.
Vitomira serves alongside Geir.
Asta is Queen of Dale, beloved for her wisdom and grace.
Val is an elder of Dale, keeper of lore and of the healing arts.
Kisha is wife to Val, skilled in herb lore.
Svedorn commands the garrison of Laketown.
Izdenka manages the affairs of Laketown.
Lashonek commands warriors of Dale.
Zheneva is wife to Lashonek.
Galden commands the southern garrison of Dale.
Zlatka is daughter of Galden.
Alvar is a captain of the Dale Guard.
Zorina is a noble lady of Dale.
Rand is a lord of Dale, warden of the eastern vales, who keeps the old alliance with the Dwarves of Erebor.
Siga is a Dwarf noblewoman of the line of Durin.
Apolanea is a Dwarf maiden of noble birth.
Ask is a lord of Dale who manages the trade routes between the Mountain and the Long Lake.
Erta is wife to Ori, known for her skill in gem-cutting.
Simir is a prince of Dale, heir to his father's throne.
Mimir is a prince of the royal house of Dale.
Urik is a Dwarf prince of Erebor, skilled in smithcraft and warfare.
Lek is heir to Ori's holdings, trained in both trade and combat.
Khadurak is the Taskral of Harad, supreme commander of the southern armies. He leads the Mumakil war elephants against the enemies of his people, allied with Mordor against Gondor.
Anidha is a daughter of the Taskral, versed in court politics.
Arwa is a princess of the desert tribes.
Manan raids the coastal settlements of Gondor.
Nuqar commands the elite Serpent Guard of Harad.
Sira is wife to Nuqar.
Razana is daughter of the Serpent Guard commander.
Thamza leads caravans across the desert wastes.
Sasaitha manages the desert trade routes.
Ghuzid commands the Mumak riders of the deep south.
Shimra is wife to the Mumak lord.
Bushila trains young Mumak riders.
Zafar is a chieftain of the golden banner tribes.
Farina is wife to the golden banner chief.
Azrak commands the serpent riders of the far south.
Shaima is wife to Orophin.
Sanit is heir to the serpent riders.
Kareem is a wealthy merchant prince of the south.
Farzana is daughter of the merchant prince.
Hafisa manages trade connections.
Zuad is a young merchant in training.
Jalfar guards the trade caravans.
Zulkhan commands a fortress on the northern frontier.
Salma is wife to the frontier commander.
Zulaika trains with the frontier garrison.
Sulhana is a noble of the frontier.
Khalida is wife to Khadurak, and a Haradrim noble lady of high standing.
Karith commands raiding parties into enemy lands.
Judira is wife to Karith.
Azina is daughter of a raiding captain.
Ukhai leads desert raiders against northern caravans.
Ashisa is wife to the raider captain.
Namir commands archers of the desert tribes.
Yamina is wife to the archer commander.
Suna trains young archers.
Zanuwa is a skilled archer of the tribe.
Hajara guards the desert watchtowers.
Qahin leads scouts into enemy territory.
Sukayna is wife to the scout commander.
Marzuk is a chieftain of the eastern Haradrim, lord of the oasis settlements.
Tariq is heir to the eastern oasis lords.
Maraa is wife to Calemir, known for her wisdom.
Akhôr commands the coastal Haradrim, allied with the Corsairs of Umbar.
Haqan is a sea captain of the coastal tribes.
Ruma is wife to Haldir, managing their coastal holdings.
Dhiyul is heir to the Taskral, trained in the ways of the Mumak riders.
Addas is a Haradrim warrior prince.
Usair is heir to the coastal holdings.
Théoden, King of Rohan, rules from Meduseld in Edoras. Once bewitched by Saruman's servant Gríma, he was freed by Gandalf and led his people to glory at Helm's Deep and the Pelennor Fields.
Elys is a noble lady of the Rohirrim court.
Liena serves the royal household.
Silvind is a shieldmaiden of the Westfold.
Lasand serves in the Westfold garrison.
Romund serves as a captain of the Royal Guard.
Morcon is a trusted captain of the king's household.
Amorcon serves alongside his kinsman in the guard.
Erdurand is a rider of Théoden's household.
Erkenbrand, Lord of Westfold, commands the fortress of the Hornburg. He arrived with Gandalf at Helm's Deep to turn the tide of battle.
Mérthú is wife to Erkenbrand, Lady of the Hornburg.
Elbet serves in the household of Erkenbrand.
Amalgun is heir to Erkenbrand.
Arthamund serves as a captain of the Hornburg garrison.
Asela is a shieldmaiden who guards the Deeping Coomb.
Elfhild was queen of Rohan, mother of Théodred. She died in childbirth, a grief that shadowed Théoden's reign.
Varmund commands the garrison of Aldburg.
Ingeltrud is wife to Varmund, Lady of Aldburg.
Cuthræd Ordlacing patrols the eastern borders.
Wulf Celmunding leads riders of the northern valleys.
Sunnifa is wife to Wulf.
Marhath leads horse breeders of the southern grasslands.
Wulfwynn is daughter of Marhath, a skilled rider.
Eleduran trains warhorses for the king's army.
Eleduran the younger serves as a horse warden.
Gríma Wormtongue was Théoden's counselor, secretly a spy for Saruman. His whispered lies poisoned the king's mind until Gandalf broke the spell.
Adaltrud was wed to Gríma Grimmóding before his counsel turned to Saruman. She keeps a hall at Edoras that the riders no longer visit.
Gudonhelda is the eldest daughter of Gríma Grimmóding. She learned early that her father's name opens no doors in Edoras.
Ingunde, second daughter of Gríma Grimmóding, tends the horses of a house nobody rides out with.
Irmgard is the youngest of Gríma Grimmóding's daughters, and the only one too young to remember the hall before the whispering started.
Lucand commands riders of the Eastemnet.
Bertliana is wife to Lucand.
Peric commands riders along the Gap of Rohan.
Reingarda is a shieldmaiden of the Gap.
Ælle Æthellafing guards the Folds against Dunlending raids.
Wærburg is wife to Ælle.
Fasthelm Morcargas commands the southern watch posts.
Morcar is son of Fasthelm.
Hereswith is daughter of the southern watch commander.
Aldric holds a hall in the Eastfold and rides in the muster of Edoras. He is a plain horseman of no great house, trusted for it.
Éomer Eadig, Third Marshal of the Mark, is nephew to Théoden and heir to the throne. He leads the riders of the Eastfold with fierce loyalty.
Elthild is a noble lady of the Eoforing.
Unthery serves as a captain of the Westfold riders.
Grimbold of Grimslade commands the riders of Westfold. A fierce warrior, he held the Fords of Isen and later died heroically at the Pelennor.
Déorwyn is heir to Grimbold's command.
Théodred was the only son of King Théoden, Prince of Rohan. He fell defending the Fords of Isen against Saruman's Uruk-hai.
Furnhard serves as a trusted rider under Éomer's command.
Thomund commands a company of Westfold riders.
Vargûl, the High Warlord of Khand, leads the fierce Variag horsemen. His alliance with Mordor brings his warriors against Gondor in the war for Middle-earth.
Corein is a Variag noble of the High Warlord's court.
Alynneth is a Variag noblewoman.
Wythuin trains young Variag riders.
Muinser commands raiders in the northern reaches.
Rath serves under Muinser's command.
Beasag is a Variag warrior of the northern clans.
Luichan commands Variag horsemen of the western plains.
Eabyr is wife to Luichan.
Pryndor guards the mountain passes into Khand.
Floraidh is daughter of the mountain guardian.
Beitrin patrols the mountain trails.
Diarbhain guards the high passes.
Aeron leads warriors of the central steppes.
Liasin is wife to Aeron.
Gawen is heir to Aeron's warband.
Aradwyr commands the eastern frontier forces.
Brighan is wife to Aradwyr.
Branoc leads scouts into enemy territory.
Seonag is wife to Branoc.
Fenagan is a Variag champion known for his dueling prowess.
Khazna is a daughter of the High Warlord's house. She rides with his retinue, though she is still a child and carries no spear.
Siaramus commands the chariot warriors of Khand.
Carfyd leads Variag raiders along the border.
Beathag is wife to Carfyd.
Taorse is heir to Carfyd's raiding band.
Fiarad guards the southern trade routes.
Ergeon is a chieftain who leads the eastern Variag clans, known for their swift cavalry tactics.
Ranaon is heir to Ergeon's warband.
Ladogual serves as a captain in Ergeon's host.
Nywin is wife to Ergeon, skilled in the arts of healing.
Melidir leads raiders into the lands of Gondor.
Eilidh manages the clan's horse herds.
Alcaea is wife to Melidir.
Kharzul is a Variag warrior chieftain of Khand, and a son of the High Warlord.
Sein commands a company of Variag cavalry.
Culharn is a Variag warrior of rising reputation.
Tegan serves alongside Culharn.
Zhamik Zhamian, Loke-Khan of Rhun, rules the Golden Realm of the Easterlings. His ancestors served Sauron, and he continues that dark alliance, dreaming of conquering the lands of the West.
Alijin is a prince of the royal house.
Bolat serves in the royal household.
Yana is a noble of Gûrtilm's host.
Abagai is heir to the Arkit holdings.
Bortu is a noble of the royal house.
Oragur leads the Arkit horse archers.
Khorijin is wife to Oragur.
Sechen is heir to Oragur's command.
Akvoth Karmian commands the southern borders of Rhun.
Chambui is wife to Akvoth.
Unagen is heir to Akvoth's command.
Amdûr Amdûrid leads a powerful clan of the eastern steppes.
Ergene is wife to Amdûr.
Yesum is heir to the Amdûrid holdings.
Lûthkan Khundolar commands warriors of the western provinces.
Tilun is wife to Lûthkan.
Chagun is heir to the Khundolar.
Vakheraltan Khundolar is brother to Lûthkan, commanding cavalry scouts.
Sokhatai is wife to Vakheraltan.
Korte is heir to Vakheraltan's scouts.
Maraia is wife to the Loke-Khan, queen of the Golden Realm.
Khurubra Mashakian commands the northern tribes of Rhun.
Jigur is wife to Khurubra.
Molluk Illnoria commands a powerful clan of horse warriors.
Esachei is wife to Molluk.
Shakhal II Shakhalian rules a wealthy trading clan of the Sea of Rhun.
Eselen is wife to Shakhal.
Hûz-Margôz Huz commands fortress garrisons along the western frontier.
Nikath Adekig guards the southern passes into Rhun.
Bagai serves as a captain of the royal guard.
Gûrtilm Salurian commands the western armies of Rhun. After her husband's death, she took command with iron resolve.
Irbo Nikathian leads the Arkit clan, famed horse archers of the eastern steppes.
Khada is heir to the Arkit clan.
Suran commands warriors of the southern tribes.
Chaghan is a prince of Rhun, heir to the Golden Realm.
Esur is a warrior of Gûrtilm's host.
Nayantai serves as a captain in Gûrtilm's army.
Temun is a warrior of the Arkit clan.
Dhila is heir to the chieftain of the southern wastes. She has ridden the dune tracks since she could sit a saddle.
Caradan is a Haradrim chieftain of the southern wastes, young for the office and watched closely by older men.
Thiqa is wife to the chieftain of the southern wastes and keeps the water tallies of his camps.
Qaban is a warrior of the southern tribes and rides in the chieftain's van.
Guaran is heir to the Variag warlord, and has waited longer for it than he likes.
Maireas is a Variag warlord of the eastern hills, and has held them through three winters of raiding.
Rodarac is wife to the Variag warlord and speaks for him when he is away at the hosting.
Boronchar is a seasoned warrior who advises the northern chieftain.
Altu is heir to the tribal holdings east of the inland sea.
Mela is the second child of the distant chieftain, and rides better than her brother.
Valathmir Mashakian is a chieftain of the distant Easterling tribes, and answers to Rhun only when it suits him.
Sevin is wife to the distant chieftain and holds his camp while he rides.
Haldric the Black Fang advises his clan's chieftain, and earned the name before he was twenty.
Cerdic, called the Anvil, is firstborn of the clan and has trained for war since childhood.
Morwen is second child of the clan leader, known already for cunning and ambition.
Eadric the Swift is chieftain of a mountain clan, hardened young by border warfare.
Aeloria is wife to the chieftain, and skilled in the healing arts and herb lore.
Sylva Serpent-Strike is a daughter of the clan, trained in both combat and diplomacy.
Valthor Scalecleaver is a chieftain whose counsel is sought across the Dunlending clans.
Rurik Fanghew is son of the old chieftain, and eager to prove himself in battle.
Galyk is a grizzled veteran who guards the mountain halls.
Forim is young heir to the northern holdings.
Orvar is a noble of Dale who guards the northern approaches.
Dakhila is matriarch of a northern Barding clan.
Chastimir is a seasoned warrior of the northern garrison.
Shagrala was bred in the pits of Mordor and has fought her way up to a command of her own.
Zigûrbêl is heir to Cirith Nargil and trained in the dark arts. His name means Lover of the Wizard, which is what Numenor called Sauron before it learned what he was.
Zimrazîn is the second child of the Sword-Lord and the more dangerous of the two. She has her mother's talents and none of her patience.
Zagarkhôr, the Sword-Lord, holds Cirith Nargil for the Dark Tower. His house kept the Adunaic tongue when the rest of Middle-earth let it go, and he will correct anyone who names him in Elvish.
Pharazîn is a Black Numenorean sorceress, and the real authority at Cirith Nargil whenever her husband takes the field. Her name recalls the last King of Numenor.
Elendara is heir to the western vale holdings.
Dagunic is the second child of the western vale lord.
Léomund Deáfringas is a Rohirrim lord of the western vales.
Voleric is a veteran rider who advises the lord.
Urundulf is a seasoned rider who advises the local thane.
Pelendur, son of Golasgil, is being trained to one day defend the coast of Anfalas as his father has done.
Barandil, brother of Golasgil, serves as a captain of the coastal watch of Anfalas.
Duinhir, Lord of Morthond, leads his archers from the Black Root Vale to the defense of Gondor. He is a stern and capable commander.
Duilin, elder son of Duinhir, leads his own company of archers and fights alongside his father in defense of Gondor.
Rosfin, wife of Duinhir, manages the affairs of the Black Root Vale in her husband's absence.
Olek the Old fell defending Dale against Easterling raiders. His sacrifice secured the mountain passes and is remembered in songs throughout the kingdom.
Varra, a noblewoman of Dale, perished in the winter plague that followed the war. She was known for her charity to the common folk.
Nimr was a Haradrim warlord who led the desert cavalry at the Battle of the Black Gate. He fell to Gondorian arrows but is revered as a martyr in the south.
Urkhun was the great Khan who first united the Easterling tribes under the banner of Rhun. His conquests pushed the borders of the Golden Realm to the shores of the Sea of Rhun.
Solun was a respected noyan who fell in battle against the Free Peoples. His widow Gûrtilm now leads their clan with iron determination.
Kuyug was chief noyan of the Arkit clan. His brilliance with horse archery shaped an entire generation of Easterling warriors.
Undul was a noble of the Arkit clan and son of the great noyan. He died young but showed promise as a warrior.
